title: Théorie arithmétique. Théorie de Galois des motifs (1965) : notes manuscites (s.d.), tapuscrit (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This sheet is not Grothendieck's motivic/Hodge material. It is a typed page of a Bourbaki draft (header 'n° 413', page '1 - 37 -'), scanned upside down. The archivist's folio number 163 is handwritten at the bottom. Most likely Grothendieck reused it as scrap paper, writing his 1965 notes on the 'théorie de Galois des motifs' on the other sides; the neighbouring pages are his handwritten notes on Hodge structures attached to places ξ of K.

Content of the page, in modern terms:
(1) A remark. For K = R or C and X a finite-dimensional (hence locally compact) manifold, a point distribution (a distribution supported at finitely many points) of order 0 is just a finitely supported measure. Convolution of point distributions agrees with convolution of measures as in Bourbaki, Intégration ch. VIII §1. Both are announced as special cases of a later general convolution of distributions.
(2) §12, 'Produit de convolution sur une variété de groupe'. G is a C^r group manifold, and point distributions on G are convolved via the pushforward of t⊗t' along multiplication G×G→G. More generally t_1*…*t_n is the pushforward along (x_1,…,x_n)↦x_1…x_n from G^n to G.
(3) Proposition 20. Let t, t', t'' have orders ≤ s, s', s''.
  (i) If s+s'+s'' ≤ r, convolution is associative: t*t'*t'' = t*(t'*t'') = (t*t')*t''.
  (ii) If φ: G→H is a C^r morphism of group manifolds and s+s' ≤ r, then φ_*(t*t') = φ_*t * φ_*t'.
  Both follow from the functoriality of pushforward of point distributions (Prop. 19 and its corollary).

This is the standard construction of the convolution algebra of point distributions. At the identity it gives the universal enveloping algebra (in characteristic 0) or the distribution/hyperalgebra. It later appeared in Bourbaki, Groupes et algèbres de Lie, ch. III, and in the Variétés fascicule.
errors: No mathematical errors. The order bounds are exactly what is needed: pushing forward an order-k point distribution by a C^r map requires k ≤ r, and t⊗t' has order ≤ s+s'.
